column1: # sweep-classes.tsv — the sweep's class list (feature 010, T017). DATA, read by scripts/zero-gap-sweep.sh.
# One row per class. Schema and rules: docs/zero-gap/README.md. Every field is required; tabs separate fields.
#   entrypoint MUST be scripts/zero-gap-class-<class_id>.sh and corpus MUST be _tests/fixtures/zero-gap/<class_id>/;
#   recall is the last PUBLISHED figure (UNKNOWN until published) and is never read as a measurement — the runner
#   recomputes it from the corpus on every run and reports a disagreement as RECALL-MISMATCH;
#   population_kind is source | process | wire (FR-014/FR-017). A class whose entrypoint is absent is reported
#   COULD-NOT-INSPECT "class not implemented" on every run, never skipped and never clean.

column2: every recorded figure (a count, a PASS/FAIL/CURRENT/DRIFT split, N of M, N/M, a byte/line/anchor count, an exit/rc N; a hex id is not a figure) stated in the four root carriers CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md QWEN.md GEMINI.md, CONTINUATION.md and README.md, every line a docs/claim-ledger.tsv anchor matches, plus every row of docs/claim-ledger.tsv; docs/**/*.md belongs to doc-count-drift; LOW unledgered figures are one aggregate per document (figures:<doc>)
column3: these are the documents a reader takes measured facts from; the claim ledger re-measures only a hand-picked slice of 10 claims and reports --completeness as unmet (research D8), so a figure outside that slice can go stale with every gate green; the set is enumerated from the files, never from a hand list of claims

column2: every entry point named by a check or debt row of scripts/check-registry.tsv plus every gate invoked by scripts/pre-push-gates.sh; a pre-push gate that runs no single shell file (go test, Playwright) is the item scripts/pre-push-gates.sh:gate_N and is could-not-inspect
column3: these are exactly the instruments whose PASS is quoted as evidence; a gate that exits 0 on an empty population or after running zero cases manufactures that evidence (constitution: a gate's population is part of its claim), and no other set of scripts is quoted as a verdict

column2: every check and debt row of scripts/check-registry.tsv PLUS every *.sh listed by `git ls-files` (umbrella and every gitlink that is neither third-party per the shared classification nor the governance source supplying scripts/gates/lib/pointer_carrier.sh) that R5's scan does NOT cover — any *.sh outside the declared scanroots or below their one-level (maxdepth 1) boundary
column3: SC-012 is quantified over every check, but R5 of scripts/verify-check-registry.sh only sweeps declared scanroots one level deep (the registry header itself lists *.sh outside that boundary), so a check can exist without a registry row and without a paired proof; the population is therefore the registry rows plus the tracked scripts R5 cannot see

column2: every gitlink in .gitmodules crossed with every remote configured in that checkout (not only origin), the helix-deps.yaml deps[].ref entries, and the pin SHAs quoted in the four root carriers
column3: a pin can drift in four places (index, manifest, carrier text, any mirror); verify-submodule-remote-sync.sh asks origin only and is blind to a mirror (carrier: design-toolkit GitLab lag went unseen), so the population must be every configured remote of every gitlink

column2: the sentinel token gate:scripts/verify-content-boundary.sh (the gate result itself, so a result with zero surviving rows is an inspected clean item) plus one PUBLIC PATH CLASS per group of surviving rows of scripts/verify-content-boundary.sh --json at its default parameters — the public repository's fleet path (the umbrella . adds no prefix) plus at most two leading directory segments of the file — each FINDING located at <path class>:<gate class>; 'on the swept tree' means the rows come from the cached result .remember/logs/zero-gap/content-boundary-rows.{json,corpus} and are used only after its manifest is recomputed and proven equal to the tree now; the fleet is the cached one, cross-checked against .gitmodules, helix-deps.yaml and the umbrella .
column3: the gate's surviving rows ARE the unjudged population the operator must read; registering them by count and path class (never allow-listing) is the only way the register can hold them without copying private text, and the gate itself enumerates both sides of the boundary from .gitmodules

column2: every service DEFINED in the tracked service definitions — the services of workshop/platform/compose.yml and every service scripts/qa-up.sh boots — crossed with what `podman ps` shows running; each running build id (workshop /api/health) or binary stamp is compared with the HEAD of the source it is built from
column3: users are served by the running binary, not by the source; the set of services is derived from the tracked definitions that start them (compose file and the QA boot script) and from the runtime's own list, so a service added to either is covered without editing the class, and a defined service that is not running is reported COULD-NOT-INSPECT (rc 2, never a finding, never clean)
column4: state at sweep time: the running build vs the checked-out HEAD

column2: every tracked basename start*.sh / restart*.sh at any depth in the umbrella and every checked-out submodule, plus any tracked *.sh/*.bash that builds behind an existence test; minus _tests/fixtures/zero-gap/, the third-party trees of helix-deps.yaml's `<path> -> <url>` comment block, and .specify/
column3: a start path that builds only when the binary is ABSENT serves a stale binary after every source change; the population is defined by file-name shape and by the guarded-build idiom, both found with `git ls-files` and a text scan, so a new start script is covered without editing the class

column2: every row of the tracked catalogue docs/zero-gap/toolchains.tsv (tool, probe, the gate that needs it, remedy, source, container_route), probed on the probe PATH (recorded on stderr); a tool is reported only when absent AND its container route is `none` or structurally unusable; plus derived:<tool> for each tool a verify/prove/registered script probes with no catalogue row (high only when followed by exit 2 / return 2 / an undet call, else low), excluding scripts/zero-gap-class-*.sh and _tests/fixtures/zero-gap/; plus a docs-drift check of CLAUDE.md/CONTINUATION.md
column3: the tools whose absence makes a gate exit 2 are recorded, each with the tracked document that states the dependency, in one catalogue file; the class derives its population from that file (a data change adds a tool) and every absent tool with no usable container route becomes an Operator-blocked item with its catalogued remedy

column2: every *.sh tracked in the UMBRELLA (git ls-files, every depth, including below the maxdepth-1 boundary of the declared scanroots), minus _tests/fixtures/zero-gap/ and the shared third-party classification (helix-deps.yaml third-party block + .specify/extensions mirrors, covenant_propagation_exclusions.tsv vendored-third-party/generated-code rows, .specify/scripts/bash); owned submodules are NOT enumerated (none carries a registry, ~1,900 tracked *.sh), unproven-checks covers them
column3: R5 of scripts/verify-check-registry.sh sweeps only declared scanroots one level deep at the umbrella root; the registry header itself lists *.sh outside that boundary, so the anti-drift half must be applied to every owned tree to be complete

column2: every gate run by scripts/pre-push-gates.sh and every check row of scripts/check-registry.tsv, matched against the sealed records of the evidence chain
column3: FR-014 requires every PASS to carry a sealed machine-created record; the gates and checks are the complete set of producers of PASS verdicts, so a producer with no sealed record is an unsealed claim

column2: every registered entry point (column 3 of a check or debt row of scripts/check-registry.tsv; pre-push gates only through scripts/pre-push-gates.sh) whose enumeration reads git ls-files (tracked only) without also reading untracked-not-ignored files
column3: an untracked but not ignored file is on disk and can be served or executed while a tracked-only gate never sees it; the enumeration idiom is readable in each entry point, so the population is every registered entry point

column2: every public record this feature produces: docs/zero-gap/** (incl. the register export), specs/010-zero-gap-verified-closure/** and the zero-gap entries of CONTINUATION.md, tracked plus untracked-not-ignored; the evidence streams are git-ignored under .remember/logs/zero-gap/evidence/ and belong to the FR-020 scanner (T062)
column3: FR-020 names exactly these records; they are written by agents under diligence pressure, which is the pressure that caused the 2026-09-01 content-boundary incident, and they must carry no credential, guessing language or private text

column2: every numeric count claim found by scanning tracked Markdown — the umbrella's docs/**/*.md and specs/**/*.md, and each checked-out owned module's README.md CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md QWEN.md GEMINI.md docs/**/*.md specs/**/*.md (the umbrella carriers, README.md and CONTINUATION.md belong to stale-figures) — of the shape <number> <unit> (unit in files, tests, test files, gates, verify scripts, prove scripts, scripts, commits, items, rows, checks, services, submodules, anchors, lines, specs), <number> `<glob>` <word>, or <n> verify / <m> prove, MINUS the claims re-measured by a row of docs/claim-ledger.tsv; documents listed in docs/zero-gap/point-in-time.tsv are enumerated but never reported
column3: the population is derived from a scan of the documents, not from the set of claims that already have a re-measure command (that set is exactly the ones least likely to drift); subtracting the claim-ledger rows avoids double registration with stale-figures while leaving every unmeasured count in scope

column2: every cell of docs/zero-gap/coverage.tsv (subject x test kind): for every subject it names, the twelve required kinds of spec.md User Story 3 plus every extra kind listed, as cell:<subject>:<kind>; gap (incl. gap:<note>), a check cell whose ref resolves to no registered check id or tracked file, n/a without a reason, and a missing required row are findings; could-not-run is could-not-inspect
column3: the coverage map is the one generated enumeration of subject x test kind (T052); each gap cell is an untested part and must become a register item; until the map exists the class cannot inspect anything and says so

column2: every row of docs/zero-gap/guarded-commands.tsv (command, source, and the dangerous command class it stands for in the candidate column), piped as probe DATA to the wired PreToolUse guard; tokens guarded:<id> and candidate:<id>
column3: the guard is the only mechanical barrier against those commands and it is upstream code; the catalogue records every destructive command class this repository's documents name, with the source of each, so a command the guard lets through is found by data, not by a hand list inside the class (FR-021, classified third-party with a reporting route)

column2: every recorded operator decision point: carrier statements naming an operator decision (CONTINUATION.md newest §3 entries), tracked docs/OPERATOR-DECISIONS-*.md and docs/constitution-adoption/DECISION-*.md, progress.yml rulings and pending-decision lines (excluding `minor (deferred)` and `REQUIRED BEFORE` lines), and Operator-blocked items in docs/workable_items.db (read through a copy); remote probing belongs to pointer-drift
column3: FR-009 requires every operator-owned item to be listed with its options and the cost of each; these are the places such decisions are recorded, so the backlog is derived from them rather than remembered

column2: every documented limitation or deferred improvement: the tracked KNOWN-LIMITATIONS*.md and decision documents (document-level members), each `minor (deferred)` line of progress.yml (line-level members), and every Operator-blocked and every Queued item of docs/workable_items.db read through a copy (item-level members); the limitation vocabulary is the decision rule for which members are findings; an Operator-blocked item also reported by known-open-decisions is one register item keyed docs/workable_items.db:<atm>
column3: FR-025 requires improvement ideas in the register with a measurable target; these named tracked sources are where operator decisions, stated limitations and blocked work are recorded, and the T081 manual intake path covers everything else; the deferred-minor lines are improvements the programme's own reviews chose to defer, so they are exactly the existing-capability improvements FR-001 admits (controller ruling 2026-09-26, recorded in progress.yml)
